chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sakuni in Kufa narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Amr al-Ash'athi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Ayyinah narrated to us, from al-Sari, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said:

Take from me a few words: You would not find their like even if you mounted your camels and traveled far. Indeed, let no one hope except in his Lord, and let him not fear except his own sin. Let him not be shy [the scholar] when he does not know to learn, and let him not be shy when asked about what he does not know to say: 'God knows best.' And know that patience is to faith as the head is to the body, and there is no good in a body without a head.
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical teachings of Imam Ali regarding patience, knowledge, and faith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* encapsulates Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) concise ethical code, linking theological monotheism with practical epistemology. The metaphor of patience as the 'head of the body' underscores its structural necessity in Shia spirituality, while the emphasis on 'God knows best' reflects the scholarly tradition of intellectual humility before divine omniscience.
